title: Motie van het lid Beckerman over een bevoegde instantie aanwijzen om ook deepfakeporno en andere onrechtmatige seksuele beelden offline te halen

reading.body:
Deepfake pornography was created and distributed on a platform without verification of consent or authenticity. The system enabled users to upload manipulated videos depicting real people without their knowledge, earning money based on views. Detection would have required either human review of content before publication or technical systems capable of identifying manipulated media at upload.

The failure was one of deployment without safeguards. The platform operated with anonymous uploads specifically designed to evade accountability. Victims included entertainers, athletes, and elected officials whose likenesses were used in non-consensual sexual imagery. It is not established whether the platform's operators knew deepfake videos were being created or whether they could have identified them technologically.

The incident shows that a system designed to profit from user-generated video can cause serious harm when it lacks both human moderation and automated detection of manipulated content. Legal remedies were available only after the fact, through complaints to law enforcement and data protection authorities.

summary:
Several prominent Dutch women are considering legal action after finding themselves in manipulated pornographic videos on an online platform that receives 13 million monthly visitors. The videos feature Dutch entertainers, television presenters, Olympic athletes, current and former government officials, mayors, and members of the royal family. Interim Justice Minister Yesilgöz called the videos disgusting and urged victims to file complaints. Managers and representatives confirmed that some victims have already reported the content or are exploring legal options.

These deepfake videos work by placing a person's face onto a pornographic actress. The platform encourages anonymous uploads to avoid prosecution, and users earn money based on video views. Legal experts warn that without government intervention, more fake videos will emerge. Deepfake pornography falls under revenge porn laws and is therefore criminal. Victims can file reports with authorities, who may shut down the website, or pursue other options including class action lawsuits and complaints to data protection agencies. Previously, presenter Welmoed Sijtsma made a documentary about her own deepfake videos, resulting in a 39-year-old man from Amersfoort receiving a conditional sentence of 180 hours in November.
title_en: Motion by member Beckerman on designating a competent authority to also remove deepfake pornography and other unlawful sexual images offline
